Subject: Procurement: SLO verification and exception windows

Hi Hannah / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get a bit more detail on how Redwood measures uptime and latency for SLO/SLA verification. Attached is Acme's standard questionnaire — the sections we care most about are:
- How you define "availability" and calculation windows
- Monitoring tooling and customer access to metrics/dashboards
- Alerting thresholds and escalation process
- How scheduled maintenance and emergency exceptions are handled and whether they affect credits

Can you confirm: do you provide read-only metrics for customers, and can we pull raw timestamped uptime/latency data for audit?

Appreciate a short written response we can include in our procurement packet.

Thanks,
Maya R.
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

Attachment: procurement_questionnaire_acme.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya.r@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: SLO verification and exception windows

Hi Maya — thank you, and great question. Below is a focused summary you can drop into the questionnaire; I also attached our SLA appendix and a short SOC2 summary for compliance references.

Availability definition and measurement:
- "Availability" (customer-facing) is calculated as: 1 - (total_seconds_unavailable / total_seconds_in_period) over a rolling 30-day window (default) and over a contractual 12-month window for SLA credits.
- We classify an incident as "unavailable" when the 95th-percentile client-observed request success rate for a model route falls below the service's response success threshold for >= 5 consecutive minutes.
- Latency SLOs are measured on tail percentiles (p95/p99) of server-side request completion time for successful requests, sampled at request time and aggregated by route and model version.

Monitoring and customer access:
- We provide read-only Grafana dashboards with metrics for uptime, error rates, token-level latency, and per-model throughput. Customers may request a Grafana read-only link (short-lived API key) or a metrics export (CSV/Prometheus scrape endpoint) for audits. See attached grafana-readonly-link.txt for an example link.
- Metric provenance: all metrics are generated from the serving runtime and routed through our immutable metric pipeline with timestamps and request IDs retained for 90 days by default (longer retention available as an add-on).

Alerting and escalation:
- We operate multi-tier alerting: platform (SRE) alerts for internal triage, and optional customer-facing alert subscriptions (email + Slack webhook).
- Built-in alert thresholds: error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes -> page; latency degradation (p95 increase > 2x baseline) -> triage. Thresholds and notification channels can be tuned per customer contract.
- On-call: our SRE rota is 24x7 with documented escalation steps; we include primary/secondary contacts in the shared incident runbook upon contract execution.

Exceptions and scheduled maintenance:
- Planned maintenance: Customers will receive a minimum 72-hour notification for non-emergency maintenance. Planned maintenance windows up to 2 hours per month are excluded from SLA calculations if notified in advance and executed within the announced window.
- Emergency maintenance: emergency fixes may be scheduled with shorter notice; these are evaluated case-by-case for SLA implications.
- Credit calculation: SLA credit is pro-rated based on total downtime in the SLA period after exclusions (maintenance, customer-caused outages, force majeure). The appendix has the exact formula.

Next steps:
- If you want, Karthik can provide a 30-minute walkthrough of the Grafana snapshot we plan to share with your security/procurement team.
- We are happy to agree contract language for the exception windows; Marissa will propose preferred wording to make it procurement-friendly.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_appendix.pdf (application/pdf), soc2-summary.pdf (application/pdf), grafana-readonly-link.txt (text/plain)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya.r@acme-corp.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement: SLO verification and exception windows

Maya — quick technical clarifications to support your audit team:

1) Measurement windows and sampling:
- Primary SLO window we report is 30-day rolling; for SLA enforcement we compute over a monthly calendar period and annualized 12-month period per contract.
- We sample all requests for status (success/error) and record latency for successful requests. Metrics pipeline preserves request_id and timestamp; exports include these fields for up to 90 days.

2) How "unavailable" is detected:
- We use a customer-route-level health metric. If success_rate < 99.5% for a contiguous 5-minute period (sliding window), that interval contributes to downtime. We also de-duplicate overlapping incident intervals.

3) Evidence for disputes:
- For procurement/finance audits we provide: raw CSV of timestamped success/failure events, Grafana dashboard snapshot, and our incident timeline (SRE notes). These are the artifacts we normally share during audits.

If you need a short export today, reply and I'll generate a 7-day sample export (anonymized request IDs).

— Karthik
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maya R. <maya.r@acme-corp.com>

Subject: Re: Procurement: SLO verification and exception windows

Thanks — that's really helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security and legal teams:

1) Can you confirm the retention window for request-level timestamps is 90 days by default and whether we can extend to 12 months as part of the contract?
2) For planned maintenance exclusions: procurement would prefer a cumulative monthly allowance phrased as "2 hours per calendar month" and require 7 days' notice. Your wording said 72 hours — would Redwood accept 7 days?
3) For alerting: can Acme receive real-time incident notifications to our security Slack channel (we'll provide a webhook) and get an SLA-graded incident summary within 4 business hours?

Also — procedural ask: we will need the Grafana read-only link and a sample CSV export to validate the measurement approach before final sign-off.

Best,
Maya

Hi Maya — looping in a concise proposal to make procurement reviews easier. Please see suggested contract language below (we can adjust):

1) Retention: Redwood will retain timestamped request-level metrics for 90 days by default. Extended retention (12 months) is available as an add-on and can be included in the order form.

2) Planned maintenance: Redwood agrees to a planned maintenance allowance of up to 2 hours per calendar month. Redwood will provide a minimum of 7 days' notice for non-emergency planned maintenance; such maintenance will be excluded from SLA calculations if executed within the announced window.

3) Notifications and incident reporting: Redwood will provide a configurable incident webhook for real-time notifications (to a customer-managed Slack channel or webhook endpoint). Redwood will produce an SLA-graded incident summary within 4 business hours of acknowledging an incident for customers on enterprise support plans.

4) Audit evidence: On request, Redwood will provide: a Grafana read-only link, CSV export of timestamped success/failure events (anonymized as requested), and an incident timeline (SRE notes). Exports will be delivered via secure file share (SFTP or signed URL).

If that language looks acceptable, we can put it into the SOW and finalize. Hannah/Karthik — if you can provide the sample CSV and the Grafana link today, I'll attach them to the procurement packet.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Manager, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
